options.text: 29 November 2026
options.explanation: This counts sixty days from 30 September 2026, the date on which the AGM should have been held. That start point applies only where NO annual general meeting is held; here one was held.

questions.stem: In addition to the annual return, what does section 121 of the Companies Act 2013 require of Nilgiri Beverages Limited in respect of this annual general meeting?

options.text: Nothing, because section 121 applies only to a company having a paid-up share capital of ten crore rupees or more
options.explanation: There is no capital threshold in section 121. The test is simply that the company is a listed public company.

options.text: It must file a copy of the minutes of the meeting with the Registrar within sixty days of the conclusion of the meeting
options.explanation: Minutes are never filed with the Registrar. They are kept at the registered office and are open to members' inspection under section 119.

options.text: It must prepare a report on the annual general meeting, in the prescribed manner, including a confirmation that the meeting was convened, held and conducted as per the Act and the rules, and file a copy with the Registrar within thirty days of the conclusion of the meeting
options.explanation: Correct. Section 121(1) casts the obligation on every listed public company for each annual general meeting, and section 121(2) fixes the filing period at thirty days from the CONCLUSION of the meeting, with penalties on the company and every officer in default for a failure.

options.text: It must send a copy of the report to every member within thirty days, but no filing with the Registrar is required
options.explanation: The direction is reversed. Section 121(2) requires filing with the Registrar; it imposes no circulation obligation on the company.

questions.stem: Suppose instead that the company had held no annual general meeting at all for the year ended 31 March 2026. Which statement is then correct?

options.text: Any member may apply to the Tribunal, which may call or direct the calling of the annual general meeting and give ancillary directions; the company and every officer in default are punishable under section 99; and the annual return must still be filed within sixty days from the last date on which the meeting should have been held, together with a statement of the reasons for not holding it
options.explanation: Correct. All three consequences run in parallel: the Tribunal's power under section 97 on the application of any member, the punishment under section 99, and the alternative start point for the sixty-day filing clock in section 92(4) with the accompanying statement of reasons.

options.text: The obligation to file an annual return is suspended until an annual general meeting is actually held
options.explanation: Section 92(4) expressly provides for the case where no meeting is held, and starts the sixty days from the last date on which it should have been held.

options.text: Only the Registrar may act, by directing the company to hold the meeting within three months
options.explanation: The Registrar's power under section 96 is to extend time in advance, not to direct a meeting after default. Section 97 places that power in the Tribunal.

options.text: The company would be liable under section 99 but no member could compel a meeting, the Tribunal's power under section 97 being exercisable only suo motu
options.explanation: Section 97 is expressly exercisable on the application of ANY MEMBER. The suo motu power belongs to section 98, for meetings other than an annual general meeting.

questions.topic: Ch 7 · Case: a requisitioned extraordinary general meeting
questions.case: Members of Purna Chemicals Limited holding, between them, 12% of such of the paid-up share capital of the company as carries the right of voting sign a requisition for an extraordinary general meeting. The requisition sets out the matters for consideration, is signed by all of them, and is dated 5 May 2026. It is delivered at the registered office of the company on 8 May 2026. The Board takes no step of any kind on it. The requisitionists therefore resolve to call and hold the meeting themselves, and incur printing, postage and hall-hire costs in doing so.

readLink.label: Read: Extraordinary general meeting — s. 100 →

questions.stem: The last date by which the Board was required to proceed to call the extraordinary general meeting is:
questions.sourceRef: Companies Act 2013, s. 100(4) — twenty-one days from the date of receipt of the requisition

options.explanation: This counts twenty-one days from the DATE OF THE REQUISITION. Section 100(4) counts the twenty-one days from the date of RECEIPT of the requisition, which was 8 May 2026.
Correct. Twenty-one days counted from (and excluding) 8 May 2026 gives 29 May 2026 — the date by which the Board must PROCEED TO CALL the meeting, that is, issue the notice.

options.text: 22 June 2026
options.explanation: That is forty-five days from receipt, the outer date on which the meeting itself may be HELD. It is not the date by which the Board must proceed to call it.

options.text: 5 August 2026
options.explanation: Three months from the date of the requisition is the outer limit for a meeting held by the requisitionists themselves.

questions.stem: The Board having defaulted, the last date by which the requisitionists may themselves call and hold the extraordinary general meeting is:
questions.sourceRef: Companies Act 2013, s. 100(4) — within three months from the date of the requisition

options.text: 8 August 2026
options.explanation: This counts three months from the date of RECEIPT. The requisitionists' three months runs from the date of the REQUISITION, which was 5 May 2026.

options.text: 29 August 2026
options.explanation: This counts three months from the expiry of the Board's twenty-one days. Section 100(4) supplies no such start point.

options.text: 5 August 2026
options.explanation: Correct. Three months from 5 May 2026, the date of the requisition, is 5 August 2026. Note that the three clocks in section 100(4) start from two different events: the twenty-one days and the forty-five days from RECEIPT, the three months from the date of the REQUISITION.

options.text: 22 June 2026
options.explanation: That is the forty-five-day outer date for the meeting the BOARD should have called. It does not limit the requisitionists' own meeting.

questions.stem: As to the printing, postage and hall-hire costs incurred by the requisitionists in calling and holding the meeting themselves:

options.text: They must be borne by the requisitionists, who chose to act in place of the Board
options.explanation: Section 100(6) expressly shifts reasonable expenses to the company. Leaving the requisitionists out of pocket would defeat the purpose of the sub-section.

options.text: They must be shared rateably among all the members of the company in proportion to their shareholding
options.explanation: There is no such apportionment in the Act. The company reimburses, and then recovers from the defaulting directors.

options.text: They may be reimbursed by the company only if the Tribunal first certifies that they were reasonably incurred
options.explanation: No order of the Tribunal is required. The only statutory filter is that the expenses be reasonable.

options.text: Any reasonable expenses must be reimbursed by the company, and the sums so paid are deducted from any fee or other remuneration payable to the directors who were in default in calling the meeting
options.explanation: Correct. Section 100(6) does both things — reimbursement by the company, followed by recovery from the personal remuneration of the directors who were in default.

questions.stem: At the meeting called and held by the requisitionists, a quorum is not present within half an hour of the appointed time. The consequence is that:

options.text: The meeting stands cancelled
options.explanation: Correct. Section 103(2)(b) says that a meeting called upon the requisition of members under section 100 stands CANCELLED where the quorum is absent, and there is no adjournment to the next week and therefore no benefit of section 103(3).

options.text: The meeting stands adjourned to the same day in the next week at the same time and place
options.explanation: That is the consequence under section 103(2)(a) for a meeting called by the BOARD. A requisitioned meeting is treated differently.

options.text: The members present shall be the quorum and may transact the business
options.explanation: Section 103(3) applies only at an ADJOURNED meeting, and a requisitioned meeting without a quorum is cancelled rather than adjourned.

options.text: The meeting must be adjourned by half an hour and reconvened on the same day
options.explanation: The half hour is the waiting period, not a permitted adjournment. Nothing in section 103 allows a same-day reconvening.

questions.topic: Ch 7 · Case: quorum, representatives, and a special resolution at an adjourned meeting
questions.case: Chandrabhaga Cements Limited is a public company. On the date of its general meeting the register of members shows 6,200 members, and the articles are silent as to quorum. The meeting is called for 11 a.m. on 10 August 2026. At 11.30 a.m. there are 27 members personally present, together with one person authorised by resolution of the Board of Trishul Holdings Private Limited (a member of the company) to act as its representative, and 12 proxy-holders. The meeting is accordingly adjourned to 17 August 2026, when the business is transacted. On a poll at the adjourned meeting, a resolution duly proposed in the notice as a special resolution is put to the vote and 2,00,000 votes are cast against it.

readLink.label: Read: Quorum and chairman — ss. 103 and 104 →

questions.stem: The quorum required for the meeting called for 10 August 2026 is:

options.text: Five members personally present
options.explanation: Five is the quorum only where the number of members as on the date of the meeting is not more than 1,000.

options.text: Fifteen members personally present
options.explanation: Fifteen applies where the number of members is more than 1,000 but does not exceed 5,000. Here there are 6,200.

options.text: Thirty members personally present
options.explanation: Correct. The number of members as on the date of the meeting, 6,200, exceeds 5,000, so the quorum for this public company is thirty members personally present.

options.text: Two members personally present
options.explanation: Two is the quorum for a private company. Chandrabhaga Cements is a public company.

questions.stem: For the resolution put to the vote at the adjourned meeting to be validly passed as a special resolution, the minimum number of votes that must have been cast in its favour is:
questions.sourceRef: Companies Act 2013, s. 114(2)(c) — votes in favour not less than three times the votes against

options.explanation: A simple majority of the votes cast is the test for an ORDINARY resolution under section 114(1). A special resolution needs a great deal more.

Correct. Section 114(2)(c) requires the votes cast in favour to be not less than three times the votes cast against: 3 × 2,00,000 = 6,00,000. Equivalently, at least seventy-five per cent of the votes actually cast must be in favour; abstentions and absentees are ignored.
This applies a two-to-one ratio. The statutory ratio is three to one.
This applies a four-to-one ratio, which would be an eighty per cent majority. The section requires three times the votes against, not four.

questions.stem: In deciding whether the quorum was present at 11.30 a.m. on 10 August 2026, the representative of Trishul Holdings Private Limited and the 12 proxy-holders are treated as follows:
questions.sourceRef: Companies Act 2013, s. 103(1) read with ss. 105(1) and 113

options.text: The representative of the body corporate is counted as a member personally present, but the proxy-holders are not counted at all, so only 28 members were present against a requirement of 30
options.explanation: Correct. A person authorised under section 113 by resolution of the Board of a body corporate exercises the same rights and powers as the body corporate could exercise if it were an individual member, and is therefore treated as personally present; a proxy is not personally present and is not counted for quorum. 27 + 1 = 28, which falls short of 30.

options.text: Both the representative and the proxy-holders are counted, so 40 persons were present and the quorum was satisfied
options.explanation: Counting proxies defeats the words 'members personally present' in section 103(1), which is the single most examined phrase in the section.

options.text: Neither the representative nor the proxy-holders is counted, so only 27 members were present
options.explanation: The corporate representative IS counted. Section 113 puts him in the position of the body corporate itself, unlike a proxy.

options.text: The proxy-holders are counted but the corporate representative is not, because a body corporate cannot be personally present
options.explanation: This reverses the correct position on both counts.

questions.stem: The special resolution having been passed at the adjourned meeting held on 17 August 2026, on what date is it treated as passed, and from what date does the period for filing it with the Registrar run?

options.text: It relates back to 10 August 2026, the date of the original meeting, and must be filed within thirty days of that date
options.explanation: Section 116 exists precisely to exclude any relation back. A resolution passed at an adjourned meeting is not deemed to have been passed on any earlier date.

options.text: It is treated as passed on 17 August 2026, but the filing period is sixty days from that date
options.explanation: The date is right but the period is wrong. Sixty days is the annual-return clock in section 92(4); section 117(1) allows thirty days.

options.text: It relates back to 10 August 2026 and must be filed within sixty days of that date
options.explanation: Both halves are wrong: there is no relation back under section 116, and the filing period under section 117(1) is thirty days.

options.text: It is treated as passed on 17 August 2026, the date on which it was in fact passed, and a copy must be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of that date
options.explanation: Correct. Section 116 provides that a resolution passed at an adjourned meeting is treated for all purposes as having been passed on the date on which it was in fact passed, and is not deemed to have been passed on any earlier date; section 117(1) then requires a copy of every special resolution, with the explanatory statement annexed to the notice, to be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the passing.
